surfaces.label: MATISSE reconstruction
surfaces.coverage: One image of the photosphere reconstructed with the public SQUEEZE code from 780 squared visibilities and 520 closure phases measured by VLT/MATISSE on 8 and 19 February 2020 in the 3.94-4.00 micrometre pseudo-continuum, convolved to the 4 milliarcsecond interferometric beam and cast onto a sphere of the published radius. The camera is computed: the rotation pole lies in the plane of the sky at the ALMA position angle, the display meridian is the sub-Earth point at the epoch, and the pixel scale is the reconstruction's. Nothing finer than the beam is shown: the raw reconstruction carries sub-beam texture the visibilities never constrained. Negating every closure phase fits the data equally well, so which side of the star is brighter is weakly constrained. The colours are a legend for reconstructed relative intensity in one infrared band, the paper's heat scale from dark red to white, not colour or temperature. The far hemisphere is unobserved.

limits.interpretation: Trial acceptance bounds, not estimates of source accuracy. A footprint is the pixel's range times its angular size, 19.6 million kilometres at the disc centre from 168 parsecs, so a contributor lies within two of those of the closest sphere point; the one-metre visibility tolerance is numerically zero on a body this size, and the sphere is convex, so no point occludes another.

derived.rule: A fixed contributor separation may not exceed four diagonal pixel footprints of the coarsest frame at the emission limit, plus the mesh error when the backplanes come from the archive's own shape model. A per-sample separation scales with each footprint's own range and emission. Every displayed point samples its closest source point.

photometry.formula: Original acquisition illumination retained; no photometric disk correction.
photometry.applicationLighting: Uniform flood displays the acquisition illumination; Shadows applies the existing fixed-epoch Sun bank.
photometry.limitations: No phase correction, Hapke roughness correction or cast-shadow recovery. Relative display brightness, not measured albedo.

display.units: relative reconstructed intensity with original illumination; linear palette display

areaCoverage.method: Deterministic equal-area barycentric samples on every retained triangle; excludes atlas bleed

observation.previewPolicy: The flat preview samples unique radial intersections only; the retained triangle atlas samples the closest full-source surface point in 3D.

transfer.method: Closest full-source triangle point; all bilinear observation contributors checked before interpolation; atlas bleed clamped to retained face.
